llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究髋关节置换术后患者衰弱与并发症及费用的关系，完全不涉及生物力学或植入物设计。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not quantify proximal femur stress/strain, micromotion, or implant-bone interface mechanics; it is a purely clinical outcomes study without any biomechanical modeling or FEA.

summary_zh.motivation: 探讨衰弱对髋关节置换术后30天不良事件及费用的影响。
summary_zh.method: 回顾性分析数据库，比较不同衰弱程度患者的结局。
summary_zh.result: 衰弱显著增加并发症和住院费用。
summary_zh.validation: 大样本数据库验证，多变量回归调整混杂因素。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the association between frailty and short-term adverse events and costs after total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A retrospective cohort study using a national database, comparing outcomes across frailty strata.
summary_en.result: Frailty was independently associated with increased 30-day complications and higher hospitalization costs.
summary_en.validation: Multivariable regression with propensity score adjustment using a large administrative dataset.

papers.title: Development of high-throughput lacrimal gland organoid platforms for drug discovery in dry eye disease
papers.abstract: Dysfunction and damage of the lacrimal gland (LG) results in ocular discomfort and dry eye disease (DED). Current therapies for DED do not fully replenish the necessary lubrication to rescue optimal vision. New drug discovery for DED has been limited perhaps because in vitro models cannot mimic the biology of the native LG. The existing platforms for LG organoid culture are scarce and still not ready for consistency and scale up production towards drug screening. The magnetic three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting (M3DB) is a novel system for 3D in vitro biofabrication of cellularized tissues using magnetic nanoparticles to bring cells together. M3DB provides a scalable platform for consistent handling of spheroid-like cell cultures facilitating consistent biofabrication of organoids. Previously, we successfully generated innervated secretory epithelial organoids from human dental pulp stem cells with M3DB and found that this platform is feasible for epithelial organoid bioprinting. Research targeting LG organogenesis, drug discovery for DED has extensively used mouse models. However, certain inter-species differences between mouse and human must be considered. Porcine LG appear to have more similarities to human LG than the mouse counterparts. We have conducted preliminary studies with the M3DB for fabricating LG organoids from primary cells isolated from murine and porcine LG, and found that this platform provides robust LG organoids for future potential high-throughput analysis and drug discovery. The LG organoid holds promise to be a functional model of tearing, a platform for drug screening, and may offer clinical applications for DED.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not incorporate any AI or machine learning methods into the bioprinting workflow; it focuses solely on magnetic 3D bioprinting for organoid production without autonomous decision-making or computational optimization.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发高通量泪腺类器官平台以推动干眼症药物发现。
summary_zh.method: 采用磁性三维生物打印技术（M3DB）构建泪腺类器官。
summary_zh.result: 成功制备了鼠和猪泪腺类器官，证明该平台可用于高通量分析和药物筛选。
summary_zh.validation: 通过体外细胞培养和形态学观察验证类器官形成。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a high-throughput lacrimal gland organoid platform to advance drug discovery for dry eye disease by overcoming limitations of existing in vitro models.
summary_en.method: Magnetic three-dimensional bioprinting (M3DB) was used to fabricate cellularized lacrimal gland organoids from primary cells of murine and porcine origin.
summary_en.result: The M3DB platform enabled robust formation of lacrimal gland organoids, demonstrating potential for high-throughput drug screening.
summary_en.validation: Organoid formation was validated through in vitro culture and morphological analysis of bioprinted constructs.

papers.title: Fatigue fracture morphology of AISI H13 steel obtained by additive manufacturing
papers.abstract: Abstract The paper focuses on researching the effect of fatigue loading on metallic structure, lifetime, and fracture surface topographies in AISI H13 steel specimens obtained by selective laser melting (SLM). The topography of the fracture surfaces was measured over their entire area, according to the entire total area method, with an optical three-dimensional surface measurement system. The fatigue results of the SLM 3D printed steel specimens were compared with those reported for conventionally manufactured 13H steel. The investigation also considers the roughness of the specimens’ side surface. Moreover, the fractographic evaluation conducted using scanning electron microscopy confirms that the predominant fracture mechanism is transgranular fracture. Microtomography done after mechanical loading also showed the influence of the stress level on the porosity distribution. Both fractographic and Micro-CT investigations confirm that higher stresses result in coarser and much more uniform porosity observed in fractured samples. These comprehensive quantitative and qualitative fracture analyses are beneficial to predict the failure conditions of SLM steel parts, especially in the case of fatigue damage. From the quantitative analysis of the H13 SLM-manufactured fracture surface topography, it was possible to conclude that the larger the loadings acting on the specimen, the rougher the fracture surface because the ductile fracture mode dominates. It has also been proven that the porosity degree changes along the length of the sample for the most stressed specimens.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究选区激光熔化H13钢的疲劳断裂行为及断口形貌。
summary_zh.method: 疲劳试验、断口三维形貌测量、扫描电镜和微CT分析。
summary_zh.result: 高应力导致更粗糙断口和更均匀的孔隙分布，断裂机制为穿晶断裂。
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验疲劳测试与显微表征验证结论。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate fatigue fracture morphology and lifetime of AISI H13 steel produced by selective laser melting under cyclic loading.
summary_en.method: Fatigue tests were conducted, and fracture surfaces were analyzed using optical profilometry, scanning electron microscopy, and micro-CT.
summary_en.result: Higher stress levels produced rougher fracture surfaces and more uniform porosity, with transgranular fracture as the dominant mechanism.
summary_en.validation: Experimental fatigue testing and comprehensive fractographic/micro-CT analysis validated the findings.

papers.title: Mechanical, Corrosion, and Ion Release Studies of Ti-34Nb-6Sn Alloy with Comparable to the Bone Elastic Modulus by Powder Metallurgy Method
papers.abstract: The development of a Ti-34Nb-6Sn alloy by the powder metallurgy method, employing two different compaction conditions, A (100 MPa) and B (200 MPa), was carried out. To evaluate the feasibility of the Ti-34Nb-6Sn alloy as an implant biomaterial, microstructural and mechanical characterizations, as well as corrosion susceptibility and ion release tests, were performed. Results indicated microstructures dominated by the presence of β-Ti phase and a lower percentage of α-Ti and Nb phases. The porosity percentage decreased when the compaction pressure increased. Both conditions presented a good match between the elastic moduli of the alloy (14.0 to 18.8 GPa) and that reported for the bone tissue. The Ti, Nb and Sn ions released for both compaction conditions were within the acceptable ranges for the human body. Condition B showed higher corrosion resistance in comparison with condition A. Based on the obtained results, the produced porous Ti-34Nb-6Sn alloys are feasible materials for orthopedic implant applications.

summary_en.motivation: To develop a Ti alloy with elastic modulus matching bone for orthopedic implants via powder metallurgy.
summary_en.method: A Ti-34Nb-6Sn alloy was fabricated by powder metallurgy using two compaction pressures (100 and 200 MPa) to create porous structures.
summary_en.result: The alloy achieved elastic moduli of 14.0-18.8 GPa, comparable to bone, with acceptable corrosion resistance and ion release levels.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing, corrosion susceptibility, and ion release experiments validated the alloy's biocompatibility and mechanical suitability.
